  "narrative_text": "Three pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, mummichog m/z-direct on human_mfn, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converge on a coherent biological signal centred on glutathione homeostasis and amino-acid/one-carbon metabolism. Glutathione (C00051) appears as the dominant driver: it is the sole hit in MetaboAnalystR's glutathione metabolism pathway (KEGG:hsa00480, p=0.0686), hits RaMP's Biological Oxidations pathway (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR 3.65e-03) alongside coumarin, and is the top-ranked mummichog compound mapped to glutathione metabolism (MUMM:glutathione_metabolism, p=0.0507). Phosphoserine (C01005) pairs with glutathione in the trans-sulfuration / one-carbon metabolism pathway (WP:WP2525, RaMP FDR 3.58e-04, fold enrichment 450×) and in the amino-acid metabolism-in-triple-negative-breast-cancer pathway (WP:WP5213, RaMP FDR 6.92e-05, fold enrichment 1422× — the single highest enrichment score in the entire dataset). Mummichog independently confirms this cluster via its glycine/serine/alanine/threonine pathway (p=0.00353, 100% overlap with the two input compounds), and MetaboAnalystR corroborates via KEGG hsa00270 (cysteine and methionine metabolism, p=0.0804). Pantothenic acid (C00864) independently drives two pathways: RaMP's water-soluble vitamins and cofactors pathway (R-HSA-196849, FDR 1.44e-03) and MetaboAnalystR's pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis pathway (KEGG:hsa00770, p=0.0494). Coumarin (C05851) contributes to biological oxidations (R-HSA-211859) and xenobiotics metabolism (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism, p=0.00353). The bromide, benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-epoxide, methimazole, beta-mercaptoethanol, and N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl inputs were not resolved by any ORA tool, but the mummichog empirical-compound network synthesised 264 m/z features — the enrichment of glutathione and coumarin across the network analysis reinforces a biological-oxidations / phase-I/II-xenobiotic-response story even with incomplete ID resolution. The convergence across ORA (RaMP), m/z-direct (mummichog), and KEGG-specific (MetaboAnalystR) paradigms identifies a treatment-induced perturbation of glutathione-dependent detoxification and serine-family amino-acid metabolism.",

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, mummichog m/z-direct on human_mfn, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA) converge on a coherent biological signal centred on glutathione homeostasis and amino-acid/one-carbon metabolism. Glutathione (C00051) appears as the dominant driver: it is the sole hit in MetaboAnalystR's glutathione metabolism pathway (KEGG:hsa00480, p=0.0686), hits RaMP's Biological Oxidations pathway (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR 3.65e-03) alongside coumarin, and is the top-ranked mummichog compound mapped to glutathione metabolism (MUMM:glutathione_metabolism, p=0.0507). Phosphoserine (C01005) pairs with glutathione in the trans-sulfuration / one-carbon metabolism pathway (WP:WP2525, RaMP FDR 3.58e-04, fold enrichment 450×) and in the amino-acid metabolism-in-triple-negative-breast-cancer pathway (WP:WP5213, RaMP FDR 6.92e-05, fold enrichment 1422× — the single highest enrichment score in the entire dataset). Mummichog independently confirms this cluster via its glycine/serine/alanine/threonine pathway (p=0.00353, 100% overlap with the two input compounds), and MetaboAnalystR corroborates via KEGG hsa00270 (cysteine and methionine metabolism, p=0.0804). Pantothenic acid (C00864) independently drives two pathways: RaMP's water-soluble vitamins and cofactors pathway (R-HSA-196849, FDR 1.44e-03) and MetaboAnalystR's pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis pathway (KEGG:hsa00770, p=0.0494). Coumarin (C05851) contributes to biological oxidations (R-HSA-211859) and xenobiotics metabolism (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism, p=0.00353). The bromide, benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-epoxide, methimazole, beta-mercaptoethanol, and N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl inputs were not resolved by any ORA tool, but the mummichog empirical-compound network synthesised 264 m/z features — the enrichment of glutathione and coumarin across the network analysis reinforces a biological-oxidations / phase-I/II-xenobiotic-response story even with incomplete ID resolution. The convergence across ORA (RaMP), m/z-direct (mummichog), and KEGG-specific (MetaboAnalystR) paradigms identifies a treatment-induced perturbation of glutathione-dependent detoxification and serine-family amino-acid metabolism.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three pathway-analysis paradigms converge on amino-acid metabolism and xenobiotic response pathways. RaMP ORA identifies the Amino acid metabolism in triple-negative breast cancer cells pathway (WP:WP5213) as the top WikiPathways hit with FDR 6.92e-05 and fold enrichment 1422, driven by glutathione and phosphoserine. The same ORA also hits the broader Metabolism super-pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1430728) at FDR 6.92e-05, and the Biological oxidations pathway (REACT:R-HSA-211859) at rank 9 with FDR 0.00365, both containing coumarin and glutathione. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently confirms the Glycine, serine, alanine and threonine metabolism pathway (MUMM:glycine_serine_alanine_and_threonine_metabolism) at p-value 0.00437 with full overlap of both glutathione and phosphoserine, and separately hits Xenobiotics metabolism (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism) at p-value 0.00437 containing glutathione and coumarin. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA corroborates pantothenic acid involvement via Pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis (KEGG:hsa00770, p-value 0.0494). The convergent signal across ORA, mummichog, and KEGG PSEA establishes treatment-induced perturbation of glutathione-dependent detoxification and serine-family amino-acid metabolism.
